items.title: New slide deck on the biggest open problems in post-training and how the field got to where it is to...
items.content:
New slide deck on the biggest open problems in post-training and how the field got to where it is today. Largely, this is a statement of my goals with Trillium Labs (not that we can do every project at once). Stay in touch if you're working on any of these in the open!

Opens with the evolution of post-training and ends with a debate on how RSI is changing this type of research.

The research areas on my mind:

1. Harness specialization and design – How do we design environments for context management that enable new paradigms of using LLMs?
2. Character training – How do we create the personality of models and how does this impact safety, trust, and diffusion of LLMs?
3. Open-source RL environments – How do we create scalable, open data methods?
4. Reasoning efficiency in RL – How do we control and manipulate the reasoning efficiency of LLMs?
5. Scaling laws for RL – How do we design principled experimentation methodology for large-scale post-training?
6. Multi-agent scaling laws – What are the main axes of inquiry into multi-LLM systems and collaborations? 

Re-recording video soon :) was from a recent visit to Cornell

items.title: Teammate on Fable 5.2 built Getsumen Express, a Moon and Mars exploration game you can play in your ...
items.content:
Teammate on Fable 5.2 built Getsumen Express, a Moon and Mars exploration game you can play in your browser at https://t.co/JrE7q1VPAY. You walk and drive a rover across both worlds, scan real landmarks like the Apollo landing sites, Curiosity and Viking 1, shoot aliens on Mars with a plasma carbine, and take an intergalactic express train between the two.

It runs on Three.js with WebGPU and a WebGL2 fallback. Teammate built the stations and the train in Blender with Python scripts, and made the astronaut, rover, carbine and alien with image-to-3D (Tripo and Meshy), then cleaned them up in Blender. The terrain, rocks, home base, landmarks and all the sound are procedural, generated by code. Teammate tested every build in Chrome on a rented cloud GPU and recorded this 57-second trailer there at 1080p60.

Total cost: about 73,000 credits (~$730) on Fable 5.2 xhigh.
